reply_construction_scope: Logical replies are freshly constructed codec inputs, not daemon-produced replies or proof of class loading, method execution, staging, durability, caps, osd_max_write_op_reply_len or EOPNOTSUPP semantics.

The public MOSDOpReply constructor keeps the request READ/WRITE/RETURNVEC mode bits and replaces only ONDISK/ONNVRAM/ACK with the explicit acktype: ACK|ONDISK for read-output, positive and eoverflow; ONDISK for eopnotsupp.

read-output follows execute_ctx without a staged write: complete_read_ctx adds ACK|ONDISK (PrimaryLogPG.cc 9220) and sets eversion_t() with the object user version (9208-9213); the logical user version is 19.

positive follows the commit path: do_osd_ops keeps the method result 42 (8205-8213), prepare_transaction returns it (9042), the RETURNVEC bound admits 18 bytes (4288-4301), set_reply_versions(at_version, user_at_version) (4325) and the on-commit callback adds ACK|ONDISK (4387); the logical versions are 11'20 and 20.

eoverflow follows the RETURNVEC bound: the CALL handler records extent.length = outdata.length() = 520 (6257; cls_hello.cc 172-188 appends a 52-byte sentence ten times), then 4294-4300 set the aggregate and per-op result to -EOVERFLOW and clear outdata; the negative result takes complete_read_ctx (4316-4322), which adds ACK|ONDISK and sets no versions, so versions stay zero.

eopnotsupp follows the pre-execution refusal: OpInfo::set_from_op maps get_method_flags -ENOENT to -EOPNOTSUPP (osd_op_util.cc 189-195), do_op calls reply_op_error (PrimaryLogPG.cc 2051-2054), and OSDService::reply_op_error (OSD.cc 1635-1648) keeps only the request ACK|ONDISK bits (ONDISK for this request), zero versions, and the unexecuted operation echo with per-op result 0 and extent.length 0.

Public claim_ops supplies input-union echoes, explicit per-op results, the recorded extent.length and output bytes. Native merge_osd_op_vector_out_data independently derives payload_len from outdata (14, 18, 0, 0).
native_decoder_scope: Separate new MOSDOp/MOSDOpReply objects receive only bytes directly generated by the fresh native encoder; native decode_payload verifies each packed union and request indata/reply outdata/result against encoded native operations. Decoded objects are never encoded or re-exported.
